text:
ida: odd one from the falcon-lite-int4 onboarding run: we're seeing NDJSON consumers fail because the model sometimes emits two JSON objects back-to-back with no newline ("}{") on the streaming path. only on batch_size>1 with kv_prefix_trim.

matt: can you show an example reassembly?

ida: sure — exact stream chunks reassembled in order:

```
Assistant: here's results
{
  "id": 42,
  "score": 0.87
}{
  "id": 43,
  "score": 0.92
}

```

ida: the NDJSON parser expects a newline between objects; it chokes on '}{' and downstream tool-call routing fails. fp16/int8 don't produce this.

ryan: hmm. is the model literally omitting the separator token or is streaming chunk boundaries collapsing it?

ida: token analysis shows int4 emits a '}' token at end of chunk0 and immediately emits '{' token next; streaming transport concatenates chunks with no added newline. it's a tokenization/stopprob interplay with quantization that favors minimal separators.

ci-bot: ran grep in canary logs for '}{' patterns, found 134 occurrences in 10k queries; parse_fail_rate for NDJSON consumers rose from 0.07% -> 1.9% on the int4 pool.

lena: two mitigation paths: 1) reassembler tolerant mode that splits on '}{' and inserts newline before parsing NDJSON, 2) encourage model to emit '\n' between objects via system prompt preface (like 'separate objects with a blank line'). Prompting is brittle though.

matt: I worry about blind split on '}{' because it could be valid inside strings. But we can safely split on the sequence '}', optional whitespace, '{' only when it's at top-level (no open quotes). Our reassembler can maintain a shallow JSON stack to detect top-level boundary cheaply.

ryan: implementable: track quote parity and bracket depth across chunks; if depth==0 and we see '}{' we insert '\n'. Prototyped on devbox: NDJSON parse_fail dropped to 0.12% from 1.9%.

lena: good. add telemetry flag 'ndjson_repaired' and a semantic-equality check to ensure we didn't change meaning. Also add an onboarding test: run NDJSON-heavy templates (multi-object arrays) across quant candidates (fp16,int8,int4) with streaming+kv_trim and assert ndjson_parse_fail < 0.2% or repairs<0.5%.

ida: long-term we should stop relying on white-space-sensitive separators: either require the model to emit explicit separators (\u003c!--NDJSON!--\u003e) as structured token or switch RPC to send chunk boundaries as structured. but pragmatic runtime fix is fine for canary.

matt: rollout plan: A) enable ndjson-tolerant reassembler in int4 canary only tonight, B) collect 48h metrics with quote-aware boundary detection, C) if repairs <0.5% and false_positive_repair <0.05% promote to int8+fp16 as safety.

ci-bot: created tickets RUNTIME-501 (ndjson-splitter), EVAL-1510 (ndjson-onboard-test), SDK-812 (parse-helper ndjson option).

ida: I'll push the reassembler change to canary at 02:00 UTC and enable debug token-offsets. posting a 12h snapshot in this thread. thanks.

ryan: also flagging model team to see if a quant tweak (recalibrate stop token bias) reduces occurrences. cc @model-team.

sdk-bot: note: if this reaches SDK, we'll expose an opt-out flag so private deployments can keep original strict behavior.

ida: end.
